tier_justification: Totality of the outcome semantics is a routine sanity property; stated so that no refinement result can be satisfied by an empty target.
plain_claim: At every width, every expression has at least one outcome in every poison(+freeze)-model environment and in every undef-model environment that binds each variable to a nonempty set; consequently RefinesP and RefinesU are equivalent to the variants that additionally require a nonempty target outcome list, so no refinement result in this package holds because a target has no outcomes.
statement: semP w ρ e ≠ [];  UInhabited ρ → semU w ρ e ≠ [];  RefinesP w tgt src ↔ ∀ ρ, OutRefNE PVal.Refines (semP w ρ tgt) (semP w ρ src);  RefinesU w tgt src ↔ ∀ ρ, UInhabited ρ → OutRefNE USet.Sub (semU w ρ tgt) (semU w ρ src);  OutRefNE R T S := MayUB S ∨ ((S ≠ [] → T ≠ []) ∧ ∀ o ∈ T, ∃ o' ∈ S, LeVal R o o').

hypotheses.name: UInhabited ρ (undef model)
hypotheses.purpose: with an empty input set, if on that input has no outcome

nonvacuity_witness: if freeze x then y else ub at width 2 in both models, and the OutRefNE form of 2*x refining x+x. The undef-model environment used (every variable bound to {0}) satisfies UInhabited; that fact is stated as a theorem in Toy.UB.uInhabited_examples (which also shows that the all-empty environment is not inhabited).
non_claims: Totality is about the number of outcomes, not termination or absence of UB; programs may still have UB outcomes.
OutRef itself still accepts an empty target (Toy.UB.outRef_example_empty_target); the equivalence holds for this package's semantics, not for arbitrary outcome lists.

The language is a toy (first-order expressions over w-bit integers with let, +, *, an equality test, if, freeze and an explicit ub); it is not LLVM IR, Rust MIR, or any production IR, and no result is a theorem about LLVM or Rust.
The models have no memory, pointers, loads/stores, loops, function calls, select/phi, floating point, or integer types of different widths; nothing is shown about those features.

No operation creates an invalid value from valid operands: + and * wrap modulo 2^w (there are no nsw/nuw overflow-poison flags), and there are no shifts, division or remainder. Invalid values enter only through inputs, and UB only through ub or, in the poison model, through branching.

Refinement is written RefinesU w tgt src / RefinesP w tgt src with the target first: rewriting src to tgt is sound exactly when the statement holds. Reading the arguments in the other order inverts the rewrite.

In the undef model a value is an arbitrary nonempty set of w-bit integers (the power-set reading of undefined values in Lopes et al., PLDI 2021, Figure 2), not a pattern of defined and undefined bits; RefinesU quantifies only over environments that bind every variable to a nonempty set (UInhabited).

In the undef model, if commits to a branch at the level of outcomes (with c bound to {0, 1}, if c then 1 else 0 has the two outcomes {1} and {0}, not the single value {0, 1}; Toy.UB.semU_ite_commits_example): it models a conditional branch whose direction is chosen nondeterministically, not a select instruction, and branching on an undef value is never UB. The LLVM 19.1.0 Language Reference states the rule 'Branching on an undefined value is undefined behavior' (while an example discussion in the same section says undefined select and conditional branch conditions 'can go either way'); undef-model results involving if therefore describe the nondeterministic-branch reading only, not LLVM 19.1.0's rule for br.
prior_art: Lopes, Lee, Hur, Liu, Regehr. "Alive2: Bounded Translation Validation for LLVM." PLDI 2021, pp. 65-79. DOI 10.1145/3453483.3454030. Section 5.2 (pp. 71-72): refinement quantifies over target behaviours, so a target with no behaviour would satisfy it vacuously; the toy semantics are shown never to produce that case.
design_question: How must refinement between programs with undefined values be defined (value-level, permissive after source UB, aware of nondeterminism) so that it is a preorder and composes through every language construct, and which candidate definitions fail?
